blocks.why: Lights out 20:30 local on a day off so the 03:50 alarm for a 06:10 report still gives you seven hours.
Straight down after the drive home to pay back what the early start cost you.
Tomorrow's report is 15:25, so take a full normal night and sleep in.
Home about 00:05 after the LHR turn; allow a wind-down then eight hours.
In bed by 19:30 on your day off — a 05:05 report means leaving the door at 03:30 and waking at 02:50.
An afternoon nap is the only way to bank enough before a second 05:05 report tomorrow.
Early to bed again at 20:00 local ahead of the four-sector 14h35 day.
You'll have been awake around seventeen hours — sleep as long as your body takes, no alarm.
First real recovery night of the block, back on a normal 23:30 schedule.
Hold the normal night; start letting the wake-up creep earlier for Thursday.
Bed at 21:00 to make the 03:55 alarm for a 06:10 report survivable.
Short nap after the BCN turn, kept under an hour so it doesn't wreck tonight's sleep.
Late report tomorrow — take nine hours and reset the clock to normal.
Load up before the ARN night; tomorrow's duty runs past 02:30 local.
Prophylactic nap before leaving home — that last ARN-MAD sector lands right in the middle of the WOCL.
Home about 04:35; blackout the room and sleep the morning, but set an alarm for midday so you can still sleep tonight.
Second sleep the same day, in bed at 20:30, because the 05:40 report needs you up at 03:25.
Only about five and a half hours available between getting home and the alarm — get horizontal the moment you're through the door.
Same squeeze again after the second 13h+ LHR day; skip everything except food and bed.
You're two nights short by now, so take a real afternoon sleep before the fourth early.
Bed at 20:00 for the 05:05 report and the four-sector CDG day.
No alarm — late report tomorrow, so pay off four consecutive earlies in one long night.
Three days off start here; sleep long and let the body clock settle.
Normal night on days off, kept regular so the clock doesn't drift late.
Same times again — consistency on days off is what makes the next early doable.
Midday report tomorrow, so an ordinary night is all you need.
Straightforward night ahead of a 13:15 report.
Home about 22:30 from DUB; eight hours, then use the day off to shift early.
Nap mid-afternoon because you will not sleep a full night before a 02:20 alarm.
Bed at 19:00 for the 04:35 report — dark room, no screens, accept that falling asleep will be slow.
Proper two-hour sleep once you're home, since tomorrow is a 12h30 four-sector day off a 06:10 report.
Bed at 21:00 local for the 03:55 alarm.
Long day, day off tomorrow — sleep ten hours with no alarm.
Back to an early bedtime on your day off for the 06:10 report.
Short nap only, finished by 16:15 local so it doesn't block a 20:00 bedtime.
Bed at 20:00 for the last 05:05 report of the month.
Top-up nap after the CDG turn ahead of the final early.
Bed at 20:30 for the 03:25 alarm on the last duty of the roster.
Nap after landing, then a normal night to start clearing the month's accumulated debt.
End of the period — a full night at normal hours to get the clock back where it belongs.

conflicts.statement: 14SEP ends 19:30 local; with a 95-minute commute you are home about 21:05, and the 05:30 report on 15SEP means leaving at 03:55 and waking at 03:15 — roughly five and a half hours of sleep opportunity between two duties of 13h50 and 13h36.
options: Ask crewing to swap one of the two four-sector LHR days off the pair
Ask for the 15SEP report to be moved later, or the 14SEP duty to be shortened by a sector
Arrange a crash-pad or hotel near MAD for the night of 14SEP to recover the 3h10 of commuting
File a fatigue report and discuss controlled rest / in-flight strategy with the captain if you operate it

conflicts.statement: 15SEP ends 19:06 local, home about 20:40, and the 05:10 report on 16SEP needs you awake at 02:55 — under six hours in bed, on top of the previous night's shortfall.
options: Request the 16SEP FRA turn be re-timed or given to another crew
Stay near the airfield on 15SEP night to buy back commuting time
Plan a deliberate post-duty nap on 16SEP afternoon (already in the plan) and treat 16SEP as a reduced-capacity day
Raise it with the operator before the block starts, not on the day

conflicts.statement: 14–17SEP is four consecutive duties reporting 05:40, 05:30, 05:10 and 05:05, two of them over 13h30, with every wake-up between 02:50 and 03:25 local — squarely in the 02:00–06:00 body-time low.
options: Ask for a day off inserted between 15SEP and 16SEP
Ask crewing to split the four earlies into two pairs
Commit to the pre-duty naps in this plan and protect them
Track cumulative sleep debt and file a fatigue report if you go into 17SEP short

conflicts.statement: 12SEP is a 14h42 duty finishing at 03:02 local, with the ARN-MAD sector flown right through 22:37–02:32 — the worst window of the body clock — and you then have only 13SEP to recover before a 05:40 report on 14SEP.
options: Request an extra rest day on 14SEP
Take the split sleep in this plan (morning after landing, then a second block that evening) rather than trying to stay up all day
Agree in-seat controlled rest with the other pilot on the northbound sector
Ask whether the ARN rotation can be given a hotel night instead of a same-day return

conflicts.statement: A 05:05 report means waking at 02:50 local, and the duty runs to 19:40 — about seventeen hours awake by the end of a four-sector day, with the last DUB-MAD leg landing after your alertness has already bottomed out.
options: Take the pre-duty afternoon nap on 05SEP as planned
Ask for the 05SEP and 06SEP pair not to be two consecutive 05:05 reports
Plan controlled rest on the DUB sectors
Arrange transport home rather than driving yourself after 19:40

conflicts.statement: A 04:35 report at MAD with a 95-minute commute puts your alarm at about 02:20 local — the deepest point of the body clock — and no realistic amount of prior sleep will feel adequate.
options: Stay near the airport on the night of 24SEP to move the alarm to roughly 03:45
Ask for the LIS early to be re-timed
Take the 24SEP afternoon nap and an early bedtime as planned, and accept a short main sleep
Do not drive yourself in; arrange a taxi

conflicts.statement: The roster prints only local station times and states no reporting offset explicitly; I derived report = STD − 60 min and off-duty = STA + 30 min from every row in the file, and applied CEST (UTC+2) at MAD/BCN/CDG/FRA/ARN and BST/IST/WEST (UTC+1) at LHR/DUB/LIS for September 2026.
options: Confirm the 60-minute report offset against your operations manual
Confirm the 12SEP off-duty time of 03:02+1 is a 13SEP local time as I have read it
Re-check any sector where the printed block time does not match my conversion before relying on these UTC instants
